facts.text: The inaugural session also witnessed the participation of several senior leaders, Union and State Ministers, overseas trade ministers, senior government officials, policymakers and prominent industry representatives from India and abroad, reflecting the strong participation in efforts to strength…

items.title: India and Egypt Hold Ministerial-Level 7th Joint Trade Committee Meeting to Strengthen Bilateral Economic Ties
items.summary: Dr. Mohamed Farid Saleh, Minister of Investment and Foreign Trade of Egypt, co-chaired the 7th session of the India–Egypt Joint Trade Committee (JTC) in Egypt’s New Administrative Capital today.

facts.text: Both sides reaffirmed their commitment to expanding bilateral trade, with a target of USD 12 billion.

As a key outcome of the 7th Joint Trade Committee meeting, both Ministers agreed to establish a Joint Working Group to explore the Terms of Reference for a Preferential Trade Agreement or Free Trade Agreement to facilitate stronger bilateral trade, improve access to both markets and promote inves…
The Committee reviewed the growth in India–Egypt trade, which increased by 35% to reach USD 6.5 billion in FY 2025-26 (April 2025–March 2026).
Trade during April–September 2026 also grew by 65% to reach USD 5.04 billion, compared to USD 3.08 billion during the corresponding period in 2025.

items.title: TDB-DST Signs Agreement with NeoSeeker Metals under RDI Fund to Advance Indigenous Critical Minerals Recovery Technology
items.summary: Advancing Indigenous Critical Minerals Recycling Technology from TRL-5 to TRL-9 16 NOV 2026 12:42PM by PIB Delhi As India expands its footprint in electric mobility, clean energy, electronics and advanced manufacturing, the demand for critical minerals is set to grow significantly.

facts.text: Recognising this potential, the Technology Development Board (TDB), Department of Science & Technology (DST), Government of India, has signed an agreement with M/s Neo Seekermetals Pvt.
The agreement will support the development and commercialisation of an indigenous technology for the extraction of critical metals through the recycling of e-waste and lithium-ion battery waste.
The project, titled “Extraction of Critical Metals by Recycling of E-Waste and Lithium-Ion Battery Waste,” has a total project cost of ₹20 crore, with ₹10 crore approved under the RDI Fund.
